question: Tell me about QueUp
answer: QueUp is a real-time civic queue management platform — join any government queue (clinics, Home Affairs) from your phone instead of standing in line. Katlego led a 4-person team, architecting the React + Node/Express + PostgreSQL stack with real-time queue updates and role-based access for citizens and admins. It placed 2nd in the Western Cape regional round of the MICT SETA National Skills Challenge 2026, competing against top universities and colleges. Live: que-up1.vercel.app

question: Why did QueUp use PostgreSQL and Node.js? What were the engineering challenges?
answer: PostgreSQL was chosen over a document store because queue position, role assignment, and notification state all need relational integrity — losing someone's place in a government queue isn't an acceptable edge case. Node/Express kept the real-time layer and REST API in one language under a hackathon clock. The trickiest parts: keeping every client's queue position consistent in real time (solved with a single server-side source of truth instead of client-side polling), preventing two people from claiming the same slot at once (pushed down to the database layer), and serving one real-time feed to both citizen and admin roles without forking the data model.

question: Tell me about SafeRide
answer: SafeRide is an emergency ride-booking safety platform built from zero to deployed in 48 hours at the Telkom10X Hackathon 2025. It adds a safety-first layer to ride booking — real-time driver tracking, emergency SOS, and trusted-contact notifications — targeting the gap between e-hailing convenience and personal safety in South Africa. Stack: React, Node.js, Express, MySQL. Placed 2nd nationally out of dozens of competing teams.

question: Tell me about BathoBank
answer: BathoBank is a Spring Boot core banking backend built with Domain-Driven Design — 10 domain entities (customers, accounts, transactions, cards, branches, beneficiaries, KYC documents) through a strict Controller → Service → Factory → Repository → Domain layering. Transfers generate two linked transaction records that roll back atomically on failure. Covered by JUnit 5 tests across all four layers, paired with a React frontend. Stack: Java, Spring Boot, Spring Data JPA, MySQL, JUnit 5.

question: Tell me about Ikhono AI
answer: Ikhono AI turns a described skill (gaming, DJing, art) and income goal into a ranked, dated monetisation roadmap — grounded by live web search at request time rather than a model's static training data, with every step carrying a source note. A Groq-powered pipeline classifies the skill and stage, then ranks steps enriched with real YouTube tutorial links, persisted per-user behind Supabase auth and row-level security. Stack: React, Vite, FastAPI, Supabase, Groq, Tavily. Live: ikhono-ai.vercel.app

question: Tell me about Sentiment Insights
answer: Sentiment Insights takes a YouTube URL and runs every comment through a three-layer sentiment pipeline — VADER, a scikit-learn TF-IDF/Logistic Regression model, and a Groq LLM layer for sarcasm and nuance — then scores a creator's Brand Ambassador Fit from 0-100 with a plain-language rationale. Includes a sentiment distribution chart, filterable comments table, and PDF export, with SQLite caching. Stack: React, FastAPI, VADER, scikit-learn, Groq, Recharts. Live: sentiment-insights.vercel.app

question: Tell me about the AI Study Assistant
answer: A full-stack study platform that turns uploaded notes and PDFs into AI-generated summaries, quizzes, and SM-2 spaced-repetition flashcards, plus a document-grounded chatbot that answers strictly from the uploaded material. FastAPI backend with JWT authentication and SQLAlchemy, React + Vite frontend, and a progress dashboard tracking quiz performance. Supports Groq, OpenAI, or local Ollama models.

question: Tell me about myCapePlanner
answer: myCapePlanner is a full-stack AI travel planner — chat with a Gemini-powered guide to generate structured Cape Town itineraries, explore attractions on an interactive Leaflet map, and export the plan as a PDF. React + Vite frontend, Express/Sequelize backend with JWT auth, deployed on Vercel + Azure behind a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline. Live: mycapeplanner.vercel.app

question: Tell me about KayJay Content Studio
answer: An AI content generation studio producing blog posts, emails, code, images, and speech from one interface, built on Groq (Llama models) for text/TTS and Pollinations.ai for image generation, with a visible prompt-optimization step showing how a raw input gets refined before generation. Stack: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Groq, Pollinations.ai.

question: Tell me about CPUT CampusCare
answer: CPUT CampusCare digitised the entire appointment lifecycle for CPUT's student clinic — online booking, calendar management, and role-based dashboards for students, nurses, and admins, replacing a fully manual queuing process. Automated email confirmations via Nodemailer, 3 distinct user roles. Stack: Node.js, Express, MySQL, JavaScript, Netlify.

question: Tell me about TechHive SA
answer: TechHive SA is a full-featured e-commerce experience for the South African tech market — real-time Firebase/Firestore inventory sync, dynamic product filters, a comparison tool, cart + wishlist, and zero-reload UX using React. Stack: React, Firebase, Firestore, JavaScript.

question: Tell me about the Student Enrollment System
answer: A Java client-server application built for CPUT's Application Development Programme — students self-enroll in courses, admins manage rosters, all over a persistent JDBC-backed database. Clean separation between client and server layers, object-oriented design throughout, Maven build pipeline. Stack: Java, JDBC, Client-Server, Maven, OOP.
